Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and and Sri Subodh Pandey,
learned Counsel for the complainant and perused the record.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.282 of 2023, under Sections 376, 506 IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station Chanda, District Sultanpur.
3. The FIR in question was lodged alleging that the applicant formed physical relation with the victim aged about 16 years in the month of March, 2021.
It was also stated that the informant's daughter had delivered a boy.
The FIR was lodged on 01.07.2023.

sentences.text: 1 account of pressure of the society, the FIR was not lodged.
In the statement under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., the victim stated that the allegations as levelled in the FIR.

4. In the light of the aforesaid, the submission of the Counsel for the applicant is that admittedly the FIR was lodged after about two and a half years of the alleged incident after the child was born.
As per the learned A.G.A., the age of the victim on the date of incident is 17 years 10 months.
The applicant has no criminal antecedents.
Apart from the statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., there is no explanation of delay in lodging the FIR.

5. Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the complainant vehemently opposed the bail prayer by arguing that as per the statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., the case for trial is made out.

6. Considering the submissions made at the bar and the fact that the FIR was lodged after two and a half years of the alleged incident coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail,
would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Ram Kailash be released on bail in the aforesaid first information report on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
